plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Late-season varieties such as Darwin hybrids and parrot tulips are at their peak in late April in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated across Europe, North America and Asia; native to Central Asia; famous displays in the Netherlands (Keukenhof) and Skagit Valley, Washington
plants.funFact: During 17th-century Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody twining vine producing long, pendulous racemes of fragrant pea-like flowers. The blooms appear before or as the leaves emerge, creating cascading curtains of color over pergolas and walls.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid April to May in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe and the eastern and southern United States
plants.funFact: Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, whereas Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, and some old vines have lived for over a century and reached enormous size.

plants.name: Quercus robur
plants.description: A majestic deciduous tree whose tiny, wind-pollinated flowers appear as drooping yellow-green catkins just as new leaves unfurl. Though unshowy, it is a key spring bloomer in European woodlands.
plants.location: Native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa; found in woodlands, hedgerows and parklands
plants.funFact: A single English oak can support over 2,000 species of insects, mites and other wildlife, more than any other native British tree.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like foliage and clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere its main bloom is in spring, but in some regions with mild winters flowering can be sporadic. In late April, it blooms in places like parts of northern Argentina and tropical areas where seasonal timing is earlier or extended.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring and early summer in the Southern Hemisphere; occasional autumn reblooming
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted widely in South Africa, Australia, and Mexico
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas were planted that the city is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', and fallen blossoms carpet the streets purple.
